about:
![Nock](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NockHUD/Nock/master/Media/readme-banner-light.png)

A combat HUD for Hunters on **TBC Classic Anniversary** realms (Burning Crusade
2.5.x). Nock measures your Auto Shot live, tells you exactly when a cast will
clip it and when it is free, and turns the whole ranged/melee weave into
something you can see — and practise out of combat against your own rotation.

## What it does

- **Swing timer that knows the wind-up.** Auto Shot has a haste-scaled wind-up
  that sits inside the weapon cycle; Nock measures it from the combat log
  instead of assuming 0.5 s, and draws the clip band as what it really is — a
  band, with a free queue window at the end of every cycle.
- **Rotation advice** for the Steady / Multi / Arcane cadences (`1:1`,
  `5:5:1:1`, the French rotations, weaves) with one clip deadline shared by
  every view, plus scrolling Shot Bars in the style of Fluffy Hunter Bars.
- **Weave bind and coach.** A press/release weave key (importable from
  Grounded), a range finder with reach-aware zones, a retry grid for the
  re-arm, and a live weave log (A-W / W-A / T).
- **Weave practice.** A workbench with a stage, lessons, a drill ladder, a
  scenario catalog, a replay you can scrub, and an expert combat log — graded
  against the rotation notation, at your own haste.
- **Cooldowns, procs, pet, Misdirection**, buff and debuff trackers, totem and
  mana bars, a React-style compact HUD mode, and a Classic layout — every frame
  movable, every panel skinnable through SharedMedia.
- **Warnings** that are worth a sound: quiver low, wrong trinket, pet training
  points, keybind conflicts, and boss-specific ones (Anetheron Sleep vs the
  Slammer, Teron's ghosts, the teleporter ALT-F4 countdown, Steam Tonk guard).
- **Setup wizard** (`/nock wizard`) and a setup check that catches the common
  misconfigurations, plus a shopping list for consumables before a raid.

## Install

1. Download the latest release zip from the Releases page (or from
   CurseForge) and extract it so you have
   `World of Warcraft/_anniversary_/Interface/AddOns/Nock/Nock.toc`.
2. Log in on a Hunter and run `/nock wizard`.

Requires the Anniversary TBC client (Interface 20505+). All libraries (Ace3,
LibSharedMedia, LibDBIcon, …) are embedded; nothing else is needed.
[SharedMedia](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/sharedmedia) and
[FojjiCore](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/fojjicore) are optional for
extra fonts, textures and sounds.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/nock` | Open the settings |
| `/nock wizard` | Run the setup wizard again |
| `/nock unlock` / `/nock lock` | Move and resize the frames |
| `/nock practice` | Open the weave-practice workbench |
| `/nock setup` | Setup check |
| `/nock diag` | Diagnostics in a copyable box (paste it into a bug report) |
| `/nock reset` | Reset frame positions |

## Bug reports

Open an issue with the output of `/nock diag`, what you expected and what you
saw. A screenshot or a short clip of the HUD helps more than a description.

## Development

Lua 5.1 on Ace3. The engines (rotation, clip band, practice planner and
grader, boss engines) are pure and covered by a headless test suite under
`Tests/` that runs on standalone LuaJIT:

```
luajit Tests/clip_threshold_test.lua
```

In-game verification on a training dummy is the final gate for anything that
touches timing.

## Licence and credits

Nock's own code is released under the [WTFPL](https://github.com/NockHUD/Nock/blob/master/LICENSE). The Shot Bars view is
inspired by Fluffy Hunter Bars by fluffymoo4kra; the weave log follows Ishri's
Weave Time Tracker; the weave bind idea comes from Grounded by Gello. Embedded
libraries, the fonts and the icon set keep their own licences — see
[ATTRIBUTION.md](https://github.com/NockHUD/Nock/blob/master/ATTRIBUTION.md).

releases.name: Nock 2.1.7
releases.notes:
### WoW Forever

- **Binds / Grounded**: a new page under Utilities makes press/release key binds, the way the Grounded addon did. One key runs one macro when you press it and another when you let go, so a spell that is not ready never blocks the next one the way a single macro does (Raptor Strike on press, Mongoose Bite on release, say). Make as many as you like: the list shows each bind's key and the icons of the spells it casts, the macros save as you type, and a key that chat, the game menu, another bind or the weave key already uses is refused with the reason. By request.
- **Breath, fatigue and Feign Death on the cast bar**: a new switch under Nock HUD → Size & Elements → Cast bar (off by default) shows these timers on Nock's cast bar while you are not casting, in the game's own colours, and hides the game's bars. A cast takes over and the timer comes back after it. By request.
- **Trinkets on the cooldown grid**: Trinket 1 and Trinket 2 tiles show whatever you have equipped in each slot and its cooldown, in combat too. Swap a trinket and the tile follows. By request.
- **Traps share their cooldown**: as in the game, every trap now starts the cooldown of all of them, so one trap tile on the grid is enough. By request.
- **Cooldowns out of combat**: Feign Death's tile (and sometimes others) stayed empty out of combat and only showed once a fight started. Cooldowns are now read whenever the game updates them, and through the rank you actually cast.
- **Hunter's Mark in dungeons and raids**: where the game hides which mob is which, the mark icon now shows the game's own mark on your target, with its real time left, after you switch away and back.
- **No Trueshot Aura warning on a flight path.**

### Both clients

- The TBC and Forever addon files now carry the same version number again (2.1.6 shipped two of them as 2.1.5).

releases.name: Nock 2.1.6
releases.notes:
### Both clients

- **Spacing between warning squares**: a new Spacing slider under Alerts → Warnings → Appearance sets the gap between the squares when several warnings are up. The default is the gap you have today, so nothing changes unless you move it. By request.

### WoW Forever

- **Multi-Shot cast bar is back**: the live client reports Multi-Shot as having no cast time, so its bar never showed. The bar now runs from your press until the arrow leaves, and follows your haste from your own shots.
- **Hunter's Mark survives a target switch**: in combat, switching away from the mob you marked and back again showed it as unmarked. The mark now comes back with its real time left. In dungeons and raids the game hides which mob is which, so there it still shows as unmarked after a switch.

releases.name: Nock 2.1.5
releases.notes:
### WoW Forever

- **Profiles no longer reset on launch**: if another addon shipped a newer copy of the AceDB library (RXPGuides does), a profile you selected or imported was saved where Nock did not look for it, so every launch dropped you back on Default. Your selection and per-character data now follow your character itself, whichever addons you run. The first launch finds a profile that was stranded this way, restores it and tells you in chat; your Default profile stays in the Profiles list. On Anniversary the per-character data moves over the same way, with no visible change.
- **Held Auto Shot on the swing bars**: when a shot cannot start its wind-up (you are moving, jumping or casting, or the target is out of range), the bar now holds at the wind-up line and dims instead of running on to a shot that will not fire, then runs one wind-up from the moment you can shoot. Works on the React, Fluffy and Classic bars, the inverse bar included.
- **More of what moves the swing bars**: getting up from Feign Death and swapping your ranged weapon restart the reload, Quick Shots shortens the reload it lands on, and a parry cuts your main hand swing.
- **Hide idle swing bars**: a new switch under General → Visibility (off by default) hides the Auto Shot and melee bars between fights. A bar stays while its swing is running or that attack is switched on, so a shot started before the pull still shows. Their space stays reserved so the HUD does not move at a pull, and they always show while frames are unlocked or practice mode is on. By request.
- **AUTO SWAP warning**: an optional square (off by default, under Alerts → Warnings) for when the game's Auto Attack/Auto Shot option is on, which swaps between Auto Shot and melee by range on its own and works against weaving. To turn that option off: Options, Combat, scroll to the bottom and untick it.
- **/nock probe windup** also logs melee on and off, range changes and that game option, for bug reports.

releases.name: Nock 2.1.4
releases.notes:
### WoW Forever (beta)

- **Auto Shot wind-up mark**: the mark drifted (reported as marks sitting about a third of the way into each half of a converge bar). The band behind it was a running maximum of interrupt reads, and one read taken from a fresh Auto Shot press on a new target set the mark a second and a half early for good. A dummy session settled the model: the wind-up scales with your reload, and the server retries a held shot every half second. Nock now reads the wind-up from your own pulls, as a share of the bar: Auto Shot pressed on an idle bar while standing still, and the time to the first shot. The share is kept per character and per ranged weapon and only moves when your pulls say so, so a new weapon steps it once and nothing creeps. The mark, the inverse auto bar's second phase and the cast-bar wind-up are there from the first frame, with a stand-in until your first pull. Reads saved by 2.1.3 are dropped at login. /nock probe windup script walks a five-leg dummy run for bug reports, and /nock probe windup now reads it back with a haste verdict.
- **Sting tiles: grey until applied**: a new Grid option (off by default). Your sting's tile is greyed out while the sting is not on the target and lights in full colour the moment it lands, so the grid tells you what is missing rather than what you have. Its swipe then drains as the sting runs out instead of filling like a cooldown. The timer stays the client's own. By request.
- **Range colours**: a new option under Range text on the strip (off by default): Text colours the bracket on the weave strip the way the Range Finder colours its segments (8-20 teal, 20-30 blue, 30-35 indigo, 35-40 purple, out of range red); Bar background puts that colour behind the whole bar instead. The weave words and the sweet spot's green keep their own look. The five colours are pickers under Skin → Range colours (Advanced), and the Range Finder reads the same ones. By request.
- **Melee bar with the weave cue off**: with Weave cue takes over the melee bar off, the melee bar no longer shows the stage words in small text; the weave strip is the cue, and the Weave helper switch owns the strip and the leg learning only. The weaving quickstart says NO CUE when both the melee-bar cue and the strip are off.

releases.name: Nock 2.1.3
releases.notes:
### Both clients

- **Settings: Step aside**: a new footer button hides the settings window without closing it, so you can drag the HUD into place and come straight back to the page, tab and search you were on. A pill at the top of the screen brings the window back and carries a Lock / Unlock frames toggle of its own; the lock is otherwise left as you had it. The same cycle (open, step aside, back) is on a keybinding, Settings: open / step aside / back, under Key Bindings → Nock.

### WoW Forever (beta)

- **Auto Shot wind-up**: the client now has a wind-up before each Auto Shot, and the game reports nothing about it, so Nock measures it from your own shots: a move that begins inside the wind-up interrupts it, and from those interrupts Nock learns where the wind-up starts (the game's 0.5 s plus your latency, so about 0.6 s). The wind-up mark on the Auto Shot bar and the inverse auto bar's second phase move to the measured spot (the spell-queue window stands in until the first measurement), and the React cast bar shows the wind-up the way it does on TBC: standing still it runs up to the shot; after a late stop it runs from the stop. Moving before the mark is free; moving past it holds the shot until about a second after you stand still again. The measurement is kept per character. Auto Shot wind-up on cast bar (Nock HUD → Size & Elements) switches the cast-bar part off, which you will want with the inverse auto bar, since the two would show the same window twice; the switch now sits in Simple mode. /nock probe windup shows what Nock measured, for bug reports.
- **Learned spells only**: a new Grid option (off by default) leaves a cooldown tile out of the grid while you have not trained its spell, instead of showing it greyed; the row closes up, and the tile returns the moment you learn the spell. The cooldown board still lists the spell, greyed, so it can be placed ahead of time. By request.
